69.text: the shopkeepers , having come back from dinner

78.text: but a few rough - looking countrymen in coarse overcoats

83.text: a few heavy work - horses , harnessed to farm wagons

35.text: the north end of the town

377.text: A shabby little traveling man , who was just then coming out of the store on his way to the saloon

quotes.text:
“My
kitten, oh, my kitten! Her will fweeze!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Why, Emil! I told you to stay in the store and not to come out.
What is the matter with you?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“My kitten, sister, my kitten! A man put her out, and a dog chased
her up there.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Oh, Emil! Didn't I tell you she'd get us into trouble of some
kind, if you brought her? What made you tease me so? But there,
I ought to have known better myself.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“No, she won't come down. Somebody will have to
go up after her. I saw the Linstrums' wagon in town. I'll go and
see if I can find Carl. Maybe he can do something. Only you must
stop crying, or I won't go a step. Where's your comforter? Did
you leave it in the store? Never mind. Hold still, till I put
this on you.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “My God, girl, what a head of hair!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“I'll have to go up after her, Alexandra. I think at the depot
they have some spikes I can strap on my feet. Wait a minute.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“I left it in the drug store. I couldn't climb in it, anyhow.
Catch me if I fall, Emil,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Now go into the store with her,
Emil, and get warm.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Wait a
minute, Alexandra. Why can't I drive for you as far as our place?
It's getting colder every minute. Have you seen the doctor?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Yes. He is coming over to-morrow. But he says father can't
get better; can't get well.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown
